issues.message: Date chronology violation detected. Admission date (2025-10-10) equals surgery date (2025-10-10), but discharge date is null (patient still admitted at POD 17, 2025-10-27). However, the extraction uses surgery date as admission date without explicit admission documentation. This may indicate date format confusion or missing admission date.
issues.suggestedFix: Verify actual admission date from admission H&P or registration records. Surgery date (10/10/2025) may not equal admission date for elective procedures. If dates appear as DD/MM/YYYY in source, verify format interpretation.

issues.message: Date format ambiguity not properly handled. Multiple dates in format DD/MM/YY or MM/DD/YY (1/8/2025, 10/10/25, 11/10/25, 12/10/25, 27/10/25) are ambiguous but extraction shows inconsistent confidence levels and missing warnings for some dates.
issues.suggestedFix: All ambiguous dates (where both numbers ≤12) should have confidence='medium' or 'low' and include warnings explaining the ambiguity. Date format should be consistently interpreted based on unambiguous dates in the document.

issues.message: Temporal misattribution: dischargeGCS uses POD 1 data (11/10/25) as discharge status when patient is still admitted at POD 17 (27/10/25). This violates the rule that discharge status must cite discharge-timeframe sources.
issues.suggestedFix: Cannot use POD 1 exam for discharge GCS when patient remains admitted at POD 17. Either extract GCS from most recent documentation (POD 17) or mark as unavailable until discharge. Current approach is temporal hallucination.

issues.message: Temporal misattribution: dischargeKPS, dischargeECOG, and dischargemRS are estimated from POD 17 data but labeled as 'discharge' status when patient has not been discharged. These should be labeled as 'current status at POD 17' not 'discharge status'.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename fields to 'currentKPS', 'currentECOG', 'currentmRS' or add explicit note that these are pre-discharge estimates. Do not present as discharge values when discharge has not occurred.

issues.message: Missing DISCHARGE_SUMMARY acknowledged in inventory (completenessScore: 7) but extraction includes extensive discharge information (dischargeMedications, dischargeDisposition, discharge functional scores) with high confidence. This is contradictory - cannot have high-confidence discharge data without discharge summary.
issues.suggestedFix: Lower confidence for all discharge-related extractions to 'medium' or 'low' and add warnings that information is inferred from progress notes, not formal discharge documentation. Completeness score of 7 indicates critically incomplete documentation.

issues.message: POD coverage is 17% (only POD 1, 2, 17 documented out of 18 expected PODs). This represents an 83% documentation gap (15 missing PODs including POD 0 and POD 3-16). Hospital course extraction does not explicitly document these massive gaps.
issues.suggestedFix: Add hospitalCourse field with dailyProgress array that explicitly documents: POD 0 (missing), POD 1 (documented), POD 2 (documented), POD 3-16 (14-day gap - no documentation), POD 17 (documented). Include CRITICAL warning about 83% documentation gap making clinical trajectory assessment unreliable.

issues.message: admissionDate sourceQuote 'Date of Service: 10/10/25 0810' is from operative report, not admission documentation. This is surgery date, not admission date. Extraction fabricates admission date by assuming surgery date = admission date without evidence.
issues.suggestedFix: Mark admissionDate as null or 'unknown' with warning that no admission documentation available. Do not fabricate admission date from surgery date without explicit evidence they are the same.

issues.message: admissionStatus.neurologicalStatus has sourceQuote: null and sourceContext: 'No admission exam documented'. This violates grounding requirement - every value must have sourceQuote that exists verbatim in notes. Cannot extract value without source.
issues.suggestedFix: Set value to null with warning that admission neurological status is not documented. Do not fabricate values without source quotes.

issues.message: admissionStatus.functionalStatus uses sourceQuote from February 2025 event (pre-admission by 8 months) to describe admission status in October 2025. This is temporal hallucination - cannot use 8-month-old data for admission status.
issues.suggestedFix: Mark admission functional status as null/unknown. The February event is historical context, not admission status. Do not conflate historical events with admission presentation.

issues.message: ICD-10 code I72.9 (Aneurysm) does not match clinical diagnosis of bilateral ICA steno-occlusive disease. This is a major coding error that could affect billing and medical records. Warning is present but severity should be CRITICAL.
issues.suggestedFix: Flag as CRITICAL coding error. Correct codes should be I65.2 (Occlusion and stenosis of carotid artery) or I67.5 (Moyamoya disease). Current code is medically incorrect.

issues.message: Keppra dosing inconsistency: Outpatient prescription was 750mg PO BID (1/8/25), but post-seizure dose is 1000mg IV BID (12/10/25). Discharge medication lists 1000mg IV BID but patient cannot be discharged on IV medication. Route must be PO for discharge, but dose conversion not documented.

issues.message: Follow-up appointments scheduled for September 5 and mid-September 2025 are listed as discharge follow-up plans, but these dates are BEFORE surgery date (October 10, 2025). These were pre-operative appointments, not post-discharge plans. Warnings acknowledge this but appointments should not be in 'followUpPlans' section.

issues.message: Missing ADMISSION_HP acknowledged in inventory but extraction does not adequately reflect impact. Admission status fields are mostly null/unknown but confidence levels and warnings do not emphasize that baseline assessment is impossible without admission documentation.

issues.message: Hospital course field is completely absent from extraction despite being a key component of discharge summary. With 83% POD documentation gap, hospital course is critically incomplete but not extracted or documented.
